newsitem.title: SPAIN: Poor gas results seen denting Repsol Q1.
newsitem.headline: Poor gas results seen denting Repsol Q1.

text.p: Spain's Repsol is expected to post flat to weaker first quarter profits this week, with good performances from all business divisions except for gas, which will weigh on overall results, analysts said on Monday.
They forecast net attributable profit at between 33 and 36 billion pesetas in the first quarter, versus 35.41 billion pesetas in the first quarter of 1996.
Operating profit is expected to do better, rising to 60 billion pesetas at most, versus 53.12 billion pesetas in the year-ago period.

At the core level, profits will be boosted by what may be up to triple the level of earnings in the exploration and production division, boosted by a stronger dollar versus the peseta, an increase in the price of crude, increased production and the incorporation of the purchase of Astra.

One analyst at a Spanish bank said: "Exploration and production will see improvements on the back of a stronger dollar, and a rise in the price of crude, but also because Repsol are now operating in more fields."
Refining and marketing may see earnings increase 10 to 25 percent because of Peru's Pampilla refinery coming on-stream, and fatter refining margins, analysts said.
But thinner marketing margins may offset part of these effects, some warned.
The chemical division should see a comeback of up to 25 percent, with product prices recovering after a lacklustre performance during the whole of 1996, they added.
"Prices have recovered, and there's also been capacity increases, so we should see the positive effects of that," said Lucia Granda, analyst at Beta Capital.
The gas division may post a 30-40 percent drop in results, analysts said, after a particularly mild winter affected consumption heavily.
Repsol's 45 percent-owned subsidiary Gas Natural said on Friday its first quarter profit fell nearly five percent at the end of the first quarter.
But some analysts expressed concern that gas results will have also been dulled by lower margins, and not just lower consumption.
Repsol will likely announce first quarter results on Tuesday May 13, or on Wednesday May 14.
